source_cards.front: A curve or hill blocks the view near a listed disabled vehicle. What adjustment does the handbook call for?
source_cards.back: When a listed disabled vehicle is within five hundred feet of a curve, hill or other blocked view, put the warning in that direction at least five hundred feet from the vehicle so approaching traffic has adequate warning.

source_cards.front: When the stated lamp-time warning-device requirement does not apply to a listed disabled vehicle on the roadway, what warning is described?
source_cards.back: When the stated lamp-time warning-device requirement does not apply to a listed disabled vehicle on a roadway, the driver must display two red flags at the specified front and rear positions.

needs.title: Other traffic signs

source_cards.front: What duty applies to signs, traffic lights and pavement controls?
source_cards.back: Drivers must recognize and obey traffic signs, signals and roadway markings.

source_cards.front: How does the handbook organize signs by their purpose?
source_cards.back: Traffic signs are grouped by function as regulatory, warning or information-guide signs.

source_cards.front: What force do regulatory signs have for a driver?
source_cards.back: Regulatory signs give required actions or maximum travel speeds, and drivers must obey their rules.

source_cards.front: Which appearance describes the regulatory examples in this part of the handbook?
source_cards.back: The regulatory signs described in this section are rectangular with black lettering or symbols on white.

source_cards.front: At an intersection marked NO U TURN, which action is disallowed?
source_cards.back: A No U Turn sign prohibits reversing direction at that intersection.

source_cards.front: What movement does a NO LEFT TURN sign forbid at the intersection?
source_cards.back: A No Left Turn sign prohibits a left turn at that intersection.

source_cards.front: An obstruction has a KEEP RIGHT sign. Which side should traffic use?
source_cards.back: A Keep Right sign directs traffic to the right side of an obstruction.

source_cards.front: What preparation is called for by SPEED ZONE AHEAD?
source_cards.back: A Speed Zone Ahead sign warns that a reduced speed limit is approaching.

source_cards.front: Which advance warning has the distinctive round outline identified by this handbook?
source_cards.back: The railroad-crossing-ahead warning is round and is the only round warning traffic sign described by the handbook.

source_cards.front: What lies ahead when the sign indicates WINDING ROAD?
source_cards.back: A Winding Road sign warns of a sequence of turns or curves ahead.

source_cards.front: What does the angled side-road symbol describe?
source_cards.back: An angled Side Road sign warns of a side road joining the highway at an angle.

source_cards.front: A side-road warning shows a branch entering from the right. What should be anticipated?
source_cards.back: The right-side Side Road sign warns of a roadway joining from the right.

source_cards.front: What condition does ICY ROAD identify?
source_cards.back: An Icy Road sign warns that the road is icy and dangerous.

source_cards.front: What does DIVIDED HIGHWAY BEGINS tell the approaching driver?
source_cards.back: A Divided Highway Begins sign warns of a median separating two one-way roadways and directs drivers to keep right.

source_cards.front: What general approach fits construction and maintenance warnings?
source_cards.back: Construction and maintenance signs warn of unusual or potentially dangerous conditions near work areas and call for a cautious approach.

needs.title: Crosswalks and stop positions

source_cards.front: A pedestrian is already crossing when DON’T WALK begins flashing. What should the person do?
source_cards.back: A steady or flashing DON’T WALK display means wait for WALK, while walkers already in the crosswalk keep crossing; an orange hand means DON’T WALK and a white figure means WALK.

source_cards.front: What conditions remain before the described right turn on a steady red light?
source_cards.back: A steady red light means stop before the stop line, the crosswalk, or the intersection, then a cautious right turn is allowed unless a sign or officer forbids it, yielding to pedestrians, bicyclists and traffic.

source_cards.front: What caution remains when the vehicle signal is steady green?
source_cards.back: A steady green light means go with caution while watching for traffic running the red, and pedestrians facing green may cross in a marked or unmarked crosswalk unless directed otherwise.

source_cards.front: What should a driver do when reaching the desired roundabout exit?
source_cards.back: Circle to the desired street, give a right-turn signal, and exit, yielding to pedestrians who are in or waiting at the crosswalk.

source_cards.front: What do the described stop line, X and RR pavement markings warn of?
source_cards.back: Railroad pavement markings with a stop line, an X and the letters RR warn that a crossing lies ahead.

source_cards.front: Where does a required stop belong in relation to the stop line or crosswalk?
source_cards.back: When a sign or signal requires a stop, halt before the stop line or crosswalk and yield to pedestrians in or entering the crosswalk, whether marked or not.

source_cards.front: How do a stop line and crosswalk differ in function?
source_cards.back: A stop line marks where vehicles halt for a sign or signal, while a crosswalk marks where pedestrians cross and hold priority over vehicles.

needs.title: Skid and traction recovery

source_cards.front: When should speed be reduced for a curve under this guidance?
source_cards.back: Slow before entering a curve, because braking during the curve can cause a skid.

source_cards.front: What is hydroplaning?
source_cards.back: Hydroplaning occurs when tires ride on a film of water instead of gripping the road.

source_cards.front: What is the handbook’s main advice for avoiding hydroplaning?
source_cards.back: Slowing on wet roads is the handbook’s main advice for avoiding hydroplaning.

source_cards.front: What steering guidance applies during hydroplaning?
source_cards.back: During hydroplaning, keep the steering straight unless an emergency requires turning, and make any necessary turn slowly.

source_cards.front: When should ordinary braking or turning resume after hydroplaning?
source_cards.back: Wait for tire grip to return before ordinary braking or turning after hydroplaning.

source_cards.front: What marks the beginning of a skid in this source?
source_cards.back: A skid begins when the tires can no longer grip the roadway.

source_cards.front: How does the handbook’s skid sequence treat braking while the sliding vehicle slows?
source_cards.back: While a sliding vehicle slows, stay off the brake as directed in the handbook’s skid-recovery sequence.

source_cards.front: What steering change follows the vehicle straightening during the described skid recovery?
source_cards.back: In skid recovery, steer toward the desired path, then reverse the steering correction as soon as the vehicle straightens.

source_cards.front: When does the described steering correction continue until?
source_cards.back: Keep correcting the steering during skid recovery until the vehicle travels down the road under control again.
